title: The 17-mag eclipsing binary system NN Ser
caption: The sky field around the eclipsing binary NN Serpentis, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: NN Serpentis · constellation Serpens Caput · about 1600 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This is a working picture rather than a showpiece. It shows a patch of sky around a faint star system called NN Serpentis, recorded through a visual filter in an exposure lasting only a few seconds. It was taken with the FORS1 instrument on ANTU, one of the unit telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope.

NN Serpentis is an eclipsing binary, a pair of stars whose orbit is lined up so that one periodically passes in front of the other, dimming the light we receive. ESO describes it as an unusual object, and astronomers planned to watch one of those eclipses as it happened.

Before they could, the telescope had to be pointed precisely. This frame was snapped just ahead of the eclipse observation, to centre the telescope on the right spot. It shows a slightly wider field than an earlier ESO press photo of the system and keeps the same orientation, so the two can be compared side by side.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (4.55 x 4.55 arcminutes) and distance (1600 light years), the frame spans roughly 2.1 × 2.1 light-years. Its light set out about 1,600 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: The frame was taken with the FORS1 instrument on the VLT's ANTU telescope through a single visual (V) filter, so it records ordinary visible light in one band, and no colour mapping is involved.
understand.eye: The object is far too faint for the unaided eye, and even this short telescope exposure gathers far more light than an eye could.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The system is very faint, listed at 17th magnitude, far too dim to see without a large telescope. It lies about 1600 light-years away, in the direction of Serpens Caput. North lies about 20 degrees anticlockwise from the top.
alt: A field of stars around the faint variable star system NN Serpentis, used to centre the telescope.
